criteria.name: Hook strength
criteria.notes: 202-char first line, inside cutoff. News trigger fully concrete (wetlands comment period, Sept. 30, KUAC) and the correction is signaled without snark. Short of 10 because 2922a itself is not named in the opening lines.

criteria.name: Mechanism load-bearing + AK consequence
criteria.notes: Mechanism genuinely gates a 30-year procurement. Consequence names sector, decision and timeframe. Two gaps: no named Alaska actor, and the AI nexus stays implicit.

criteria.name: Layer fidelity
criteria.notes: All four layers present, no confabulation. Two actors rendered slightly loosely: the EO 11990 bullet omits the 'exercised through the EIAP delegation' qualifier, and the 2922a bullet defers SecAF-proposes/SecDef-approves to the next paragraph.

criteria.name: Chokepoint clarity
criteria.notes: One layer (2922a(b)), one actor (Secretary of Defense), one binary, quoted verbatim, asymmetry stated explicitly. Matches the dossier's why_asymmetric.

criteria.name: Structural read
criteria.notes: Real position, not a neutral explainer. The visible gate is routed to a committee at a MAJCOM-picked level and is 'built to survive'; the hard gate is upstream. Slightly compressed versus the dossier.

criteria.name: Forward implication
criteria.notes: Concrete reclassification instruction, a horizon (2030) and a live date (Sept. 30). Does not name who is positioned versus who is not.

criteria.name: Primary-source quality
criteria.notes: All four layers trace to primary records: 32 CFR 989.15, EO 11990 at archives.gov, uscode.house.gov for 2922a, Oklo FY2025 10-K on sec.gov. Chokepoint citation primary and verbatim.

criteria.name: Voice match
criteria.notes: Analytical and position-taking like post_001, but bullets 1 to 3 drift toward statutory-abstract cadence, and Alaska arrives late. See post_grading_revision below — the specific defect cited was fixed after grading.

criteria.name: Readability (LinkedIn)
criteria.notes: Tight 2-to-4 sentence paragraphs, well-formed 4-item bullet block. Bullets at the long edge of single-clause.

criteria.name: Engagement question
criteria.notes: Debatable and tied to the chokepoint by name. No CTA, no rhetorical softener.

hard_fail_checks.notes: Four body layers map 1:1 to layers[] with matching controlling actors. No invented layers.

hard_fail_checks.notes: Specific: 2922a(b), Secretary of Defense, binary approve/do-not, quoted verbatim. No generic stand-in.

one_sentence_fix: Rewrite the first three layer bullets as plain-language sentences with real verbs and subjects, replacing the dangling 'Air Force Environmental Protection Committee, not a named officer' fragment.
do_not_publish_audit: All 17 entries checked by the scorer independently. No trips. Tense held throughout, no NRC docket, 5 MW not 75 MWe, no Pub. L. 115-232, no named FONPA/FONSI signer, no DLA Energy, no solicitation number, no dollar figure, Sept. 30 attributed to KUAC, EA-versus-EIS kept conditional.
post_grading_revision: The post scored 8.6 with ship true and no hard fail, so no revision was required. The scorer's one_sentence_fix targeting the weakest criterion (Voice match) was nonetheless applied afterward as single-pass polish: bullet 1's dangling fragment became a full clause ('the Environmental Assessment and an unsigned Finding of No Significant Impact go public for at least 30 days, and approval rests with the Air Force Environmental Protection Committee, not a named officer'). The shipped post is therefore marginally better than the graded version. All hard-fail checks were re-verified mechanically after the edit and still pass at 474 words and 2976 characters. No re-score cycle was consumed, since the additional cycles the routine allows are reserved for below-threshold outcomes.
